blocks.value: **Compound statements**, or blocks of statements, are any statements grouped together within curly braces:
A compound statement consists of a sequence of statements enclosed in braces. This is what lets a branch do more than one thing:

blocks.title: Java allows you to omit the braces when a branch holds exactly one statement. Do not

blocks.value: The indentation says both lines are conditional. Only the first one is. Always use braces, even for a single statement, this bug is invisible during review and has caused real security incidents.

A variable declared inside a block exists only inside that block. This is its **scope**. Using it after the closing brace is a compile error, so declare a variable *before* the block if you need it afterwards:
